appraisal_events.evidence: « je n'en suis pas plus fière pour cela », dit en riant Mme de Guermantes, heureuse pourtant, puisqu'on parlait de cette actrice, de faire savoir qu'elle avait eu la primeur de ses ridicules.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator undercuts the duchess's professed indifference by revealing she is secretly pleased to publicize that she was first to discover the actress's absurdities, exposing a small vanity beneath her performed modesty.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Formidablement riche dans un monde où on l'est de moins en moins », greeted by all with easy deference, « d'une grande beauté ... comme quelque dieu grec »; but also « la vanité du grand seigneur était doublée de celle de l'homme d'argent » and his womanizing « faisaient le malheur de la sienne ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator portrays the duc's entrance as effortlessly dominant, wealthy, admired and physically striking, while also explicitly flagging his money-conscious vanity and the unhappiness his infidelities caused his wife.

status_effects.explanation: Her modest disclaimer is exposed by the narrator as covering real satisfaction at having discovered the actress's ridiculousness first, slightly lowering how sincere she appears.
He moves through the brilliant assembly with total ease and universal deference, singled out as wealthy, admired, and physically remarkable.
The narrator explicitly exposes his vanity as a moneyed man and notes his infidelities made his wife unhappy, qualifying the otherwise admiring portrait.

ambiguities: The narrated portrait of the duc de Guermantes mixes admiring social elevation (wealth, ease, physical beauty) with explicit narrator criticism of his vanity and infidelities, so the passage does not resolve into a single clear positive or negative movement.

The actress disparaged by the duchesse is referred to only as 'l'amie de Robert' / 'cette actrice', a descriptor-identified unnamed figure not among the reviewed unnamed entities on the reference sheet, so she is omitted from characters_present and treated only as evidence for the duchesse's own characterization.
